correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3 and every supported symmetric stochastic P, orbit averaging does not increase norm(P-J); the two-weight spectrum is 1, 1-2b, and 1-b-ma/2 +/- sqrt(b^2+(ma/2)^2), each contrast eigenvalue multiplicity m-1. The larger contrast eigenvalue is at least the explicitly minimized one-variable bound. Its derivative sign is strictly increasing and crosses zero exactly once. At the chosen weights, 0<b<1/2 and lambda_plus+lambda_minus=(m-2)(1-b)/(m-1)>0, so no negative eigenvalue obstructs attainment. The heuristic and limiting formulas are exact. The delivered verify.py was run and printed the supplied VERIFY_OK line, verifying finite spectra and feasible competitors without replacing the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2004 general FMMC SDP and 2007 symmetry paper yield methodology, not the exact closed corona optimum. A much closer 2020 paper explicitly treats complete-cored symmetric stars, but its displayed simple optimal weights are under (m-1) pi1<=pi0, which fails at uniform masses for m>=3. Its full-text Section 7.4 and Appendix E instead reduce the problem to a path-related optimization. The present work supplies a closed formula and full asymptotic heuristic-gap law for that excluded regime. Actual published-finding corpus searches found only unrelated graph-corona and different-graph mixing claims. The implicit reduction creates a documented residual risk, and exhaustive literature uniqueness is not claimed.
residual_risks: The 2020 CCS-star path reduction can implicitly compute the m>=3 optimum. A prior author may have algebraically specialized that reduction elsewhere without indexing.

The published CCS-star text contains a generic n=1 expression near conditional formulas, potentially leading to ambiguity about its intended coverage. Only the explicitly stated feasibility hypothesis is used in the scientific comparison.
Mathematical databases and web search are not exhaustive; unindexed specialized mixing-chain literature may have equivalent weights.

value.rationale: One private leaf per clique vertex is an intrinsically motivated dense-core/sparse-periphery mixing network. The sharp global optimizer is not a chosen arbitrary numerical slice: it gives exact edge probabilities, active core self-loop constraints, asymptotic SLEM 4/5, and an m/5 growing spectral-gap separation from both standard edge-weight heuristics, on the entire m>=3 infinite family. This is a meaningful complete natural classification; no claim that qualitative heuristic failure is newly discovered.
